1  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident. 
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as follows:
That on 22.01.2019 at about 6.45 p.m., when the petitioner was a pillion rider in motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 along with the rider i.e., her husband on Panchanahalli-Singatagere Road, from her native place and when they reached near Veterinary hospital, at that time, one motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-18-EE-9178 being driven by its rider, came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner without caring human safety and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, due to this impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. She was taken to Government Hospital,
Panchanahalli, and thereafter she was shifted to Mangala Hospital, Hassan where she was treated for grievous injuries. A case was registered in Crime No.5/2019 at Panchanahalli Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC against the rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing No.KA-13-EH-5721. 
Hence, this petition for compensation. 
3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondent No.3 appeared through its Counsel and filed written statement. The respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent and hence, placed exparte. 
The third respondent has denied the entire petition averments as false. The issuance of the policy is admitted, but the liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy. Accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 by its rider wherein the petitioner was a pillion rider and the police after due investigation, have filed chargesheet against the said rider. The petitioner has admitted that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 by its rider and hence, the respondent No.3 is not a necessary party to this proceedings. The insured i.e.,
the 2nd respondent has not informed about the alleged accident or any cause of action against the said policy of insurance to the 3 rd respondent. The second respondent and the jurisdictional police have not complied with the mandatory requirements of M.V.Act as required under Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the M.V.Act. The amount claimed in the petition is highly exaggerated and has been made baselessly. Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition. 
4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-18-EE-9178 by its rider dashed to the petitioner who was going as pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-EH-5721 and she sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 22.01.2019 ? 
Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
2 2. Whether the respondent No.3 proves that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-EH- 5721 ?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4 . What order? 
5. On behalf of the petitioner, she got herself examined as PW-1 and one witness was examined as PW- 2 and got marked Exhibits P.1 to P.67. The respondent No.3 got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents at Exs.R.1 & R.2.
6. Heard the arguments of both sides. 
7. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... Partly In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly In the Affirmative Issue No.3 ... Partly in affirmative, awarding compensation of Rs.3,89,000/-
 Issue No.4 ... As per final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS 8. Issue Nos.1 and 2: Since these issues involve common discussion, I have taken them together. 
The petitioner in order to prove her case has placed reliance on her oral evidence and documentary evidence as per Exs.P.1 to P.8, such as FIR, Complaint, Crime detail form with spot panchanama,
spot sketch, property seizure memo, IMV Report, Wound Certificate and charge shet.. PW-1 being the petitioner and the injured, in her affidavit evidence has narrated the manner in which she met with an accident and the accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18-EE-9178. The respondent No.2 being the owner of the said motorcycle has remained exparte. The first respondent being the owner of the motorcycle in which the petitioner was a pillion rider has remained exparte. The third respondent being the insurer of the second respondent, has contended that the jurisdictional police after due investigation have filed chargesheet against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 i.e., against the first respondent and as such, accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 by the husband of the petitioner i.e., the first respondent. Let us consider the evidence placed by the parties to decide these issues. 
9. PW.1 in her affidavit evidence has deposed that on 22.01.2019 at about 6.45 p.m., when she was moving as a pillion rider in the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 along with the rider i.e., her husband, on Panchanahalli-Singatagere road from Kasavanahalli towards Panchanahalli and when they reached Veterinary Hospital, at that time, motorcycle bearing Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
3 registration No.KA-18-EE-9178 which was coming from opposite direction has hit her motorcycle due to the rash and negligent riding of the said motorcycle by its rider and there was head-on-collision between both the vehicles and as such, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries. The third respondent has placed the evidence of its official as RW.1 and RW.1 has deposed that the rider of the insured motorcycle was not responsible for the alleged accident, since the police have filed chargesheet against the first respondent who was the rider of the motorcycle in which the petitioner was a pillion rider and accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the first respondent. The evidence of RW.1 is mainly based on the police documents. 
10. Ex.P.1 is the FIR lodged against the first respondent who was the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 on the basis of the complaint lodged by one Kirankumar. This Kirankumar is none other than the second respondent in the petition. The second respondent has lodged complaint to the police on 03.02.2019 for the accident alleged to have been met by him on 22.01.2019. In the complaint, the second respondent has stated that when he was moving on his motorcycle bearing reg. No.KA-18-EE-9178 in front of veterinary hospital on the left side of Singatagere road, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EH- 5721 who came from Singatagere has hit his motorcycle by riding it in rash and negligent manner and due to it, he fell down and sustained injuries and even the pillion rider on the offending motorcycle also sustained injuries and he was shifted to Panchanahalli hospital at Hassan and then he was shifted to Seetabhatheeja hospital at Bengaluru. 
11. In the complaint, complainant has stated that as he was engaged in taking treatment in several hospitals, after taking treatment he has lodged the complaint and thus there is delay in lodging the complaint. It is noticed that though the petitioner alleges that she met with an accident due to rash and negligent act on the part of the second respondent, but she has not lodged any complaint to the police immediately after the accident. Even the husband of the petitioner i.e., the first respondent has not lodged any complaint to the police immediately after the accident. There is no explanation from the side of the petitioner and her husband in this regard. Only after more than 10 days of the accident, the second respondent has lodged the complaint relating to the accident. 
12. As per PW.1 herself, there was head-on-collision between both the motorcycles. PW.1 has pleaded ignorance about the width of the road on which accident took place, but according to her,
two vehicles can pass at a time on the said road. PW.1 in her cross-examination has admitted that the police have registered a case against the rider of the motorcycle in which she was proceeding as a pillion rider at the time of accident and the chargesheet is filed against the respondent No.1 regarding the accident, stating that the first respondent was not having DL and his motorcycle was not having Insurance policy at the time of accident. These versions of PW.1 supports the polic documents produced by her. 
13. Exs.P.3 and P.4 are the spot mahazar and the spot sketch which reveals the state of affairs at the accident spot. As per these documents, the place of accident is in front of veterinary hospital of Panchanahalli situated on Singatagere-Panchanahalli road. As per the mahazar and the sketch, the width of the said road is about 18ft., and the place of accident is on the left side of the road and it is situated at about 7ft., from the edge of the tar road. According to the complainant, he was moving Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
4 from the side of Panchanahalli towards Singatagere and at that time, accident took place. Whereas,
the petitioner alleges that when she and her husband were moving on the motorcycle from Singatagere towards Panchanahalli, this accident has occurred. By considering these versions of PW.1 and the complainant and also from Exs.P.3 and P.4, it can be said that both the vehicles were moving in opposite direction on Singatagere-Panchanahalli road. Exs . P.3 and P.4 disclose that the complainant i.e., the second respondent was moving on the left side of the road, whereas the first respondent was moving on his motorcycle in the middle of the road and at that time, accident has occurred. 
14. Ex . P.5 discloses that both the motorcycles involved in the accident were seized by the police. 
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report wherein damages caused to both the motorcycles are mentioned. As per Ex.P.6, front head light glass at center pierced and holed, front D type crash guard at right side outer surface scrubbed and these damages are in respect of the motorcycle of the husband of the petitioner i.e., the first respondent. The front crash guard at right side bend, gear lever bend, front brake lever cut, right side body scrubbed here and there and these damages are caused to the motorcycle of the second respondent. Thus, the front portion of both the motorcycles are damaged in accident. RW.1 in his cross- examination has admitted that accident took place due to head-on-collision between both the motorcycles and as per IMV report, both the motorcycles are damaged. Hence, it can be said that there was head-on-collision between both the vehicles. 
If really the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the complainant i.e., the second respondent, then, the first respondent being the husband of the petitioner, would have challenged the charge sheet filed against him. But the first respondent has not challenged the chargesheet. This conduct of the first respondent enables the court to hold that as the accident took place due to his negligence also, he has remained silent. Even this fact creates doubt about the case put forth by the petitioner regarding occurring of the accident solely due to the negligence of the second respondent. It is the bounden duty of both the riders to ride the motorcycles by observing the vehicles moving on the road by taking care and caution. But, in the present case, both the riders of the motorcycles have ridden their motorcycles without taking any care and caution and this has resulted in head-on-collision between both the motorcycles. The documents placed before the court clearly establish that there was head-on-collision between both the motorcycles and as such, both the riders of the motorcycles are negligent in causing the accident.
16. Ex.P.8 is the chargesheet filed against the first respondent by alleging that due to his negligence,
accident took place and also he was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-AH-5721 without DL and without having insurance to the said motorcycle. PW.1 has admitted about filing of chargesheet against her husband for not having DL and for not having policy of insurance at the time of accident. Hence, from the evidence available on record, it can be said that as the first respondent was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-AH-5721 in rash and negligent manner without having DL, he is at fault in causing the accident. 
17. As per PW.1 and RW.1, there was head-on- collision between both the motorcycles. Hence, it can be said that both the riders of the motorcycles have contributed negligence in causing of the accident. Wound certificate-Ex.P.7 discloses that the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
5 accident. Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of both the motorcycles i.e., both the respondents No.1 and 2 in causing the accident. As such, contributory negligence is fixed at the ratio of 50:50 among the riders of both the motorcycles i.e., respondents No.1 and 2 respectively. Accordingly I answer Issue Nos.1 & 2 partly in the affirmative. 
18. ISSUE No.3:
(a). Pain and Agony:
Wound certificate-Ex.P.7 disclose that the petitioner has sustained lacerated wound over left parietal region, CT scan of the brain discloses that the petitioner has suffered left occipital EDH with left temporal contusion. As per the opinion of the doctor, the said injury is grievous in nature. Discharge Summary at Ex.P.10 and case sheet at Ex.P.66 discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment in Mangala Hospital,
Hassan as an inpatient from 22.01.2019 to 30.01.2019 and she has undergone left occipital craniotomy and EDH evacuation and bone replacement in Mangala Hospital, for the injury sustained in the accident. X-rays and CT scan films and reports at Exs.P.60 to P.64 confirms the sustaining of the head injury by the petitioner as mentioned in the wound certificate. The injury sustained by the petitioner requires minimum three months treatment. During the treatment period,
the petitioner has suffered lot of pain and agony. As such, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head pain and agony. 
(b). Medical Expenses (including conveyance, attendant charges and extra nourishment):
PW-1 has deposed that, she has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards hospitalisation, medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses. In support of her evidence, she has produced discharge bill, advance receipts, medical bills, prescriptions as per Exs.P.11 to P.58. Exs. P.11 to P.31 are amounting to Rs.1,95,194/-. Ex . P.11 is the discharge bill of Mangala Hospital, amounting to Rs.1,65,747/-. 
Exs.P.12 to P.16 are the advance receipts for having paid advance amount to the hospital by the petitioner towards hospital charges. Hence, it can be said that the petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.1,65,747/- towards her treatment in Mangala Hospital. Except Ex.P.18 and P.19, the other medical bills are pharmacy bills and they do not contain the signature of the person who has issued them and the seal of the shop. PW.1 in her cross-examination has admitted that the medicines were purchased from the pharmacy of the hospital when she was treated as inpatient at Mangala Hospital. That means, some of the medicines purchased under the pharmacy bills are included in final inpatient bill. Hence, it is not possible to believe that the petitioner has spent the amount claimed under pharmacy bills towards medicines. However, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the type of treatment undergone by the petitioner and number of Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
6 days of her admission in Mangala Hospital, it can be said that the petitioner has spent some amount towards medicines, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges. As such, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head medical expenses, conveyance,
nourishment and attendant charges. 
(c) Loss of income during the treatment period: 
PW-1 has deposed that, prior to the accident she was working as a tailor and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but due to the accident, she was not able to do the said work and lost her income. Except the oral assertion of PW.1, no materials are placed in proof of her avocation and the income. As such, in the absence of any materials before the Court to show the avocation and income of the petitioner, notional income has to be taken into consideration as per the Minimum Wages Act. Accordingly, the notional income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.13,000/-p.m., as the accident has occurred in the year 2020. The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires 3 months treatment. During that period, the petitioner was unable to do any work. Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.39,000/- under the head loss of income during the period of treatment. 
(d) Future loss of earning capacity: 
PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to stand for long time, unable to climb stairs, unable to walk for long distance, unable to concentrate on her work, she cannot study, she gets head ache often and she has sustained loss of future progress and loss of happiness. Except the oral assertion of PW.1, there is no evidence of the doctor to prove that the petitioner suffers from permanent disability affecting her future earning capacity. In the absence of the evidence of the doctor, it is not possible to hold that the petitioner suffers from permanent disability affecting her future earning capacity. As such, no amount is awarded under this head. 
 (e) Towards unhappiness and loss of amenities:
PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to stand for long time, unable to climb stairs, unable to walk for long distance, unable to concentrate on her work, she cannot study, she gets head ache often and she has sustained loss of future progress and loss of happiness. PW.1 has also deposed that due to the accidental injuries, she has suffered loss of physical and mental happiness, loss of amenities, loss of future prospects and her life span has been decreased and she has suffered pain and agony and she is unable to do any work. These difficulties stated by PW.1 will definitely cause unhappiness and discomfort to the petitioner while doing Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
7 her normal activities and also while doing her avocation . Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.75,000/- under this head of unhappiness and loss of amenities. 
19. In view of the reasons stated above, in all the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No.
a. Pain and Agony Rs. 75,000-00 b. Medical Expenses (conveyance, Rs. 2,00,000-00  nourishment and attendant  charges)
c. Loss of income during the Rs. 39,000-00  treatment and rest period d. Unhappiness and loss of Rs. 75,000-00  amenities  TOTAL Rs. 3,89,000-00 Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,89,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till deposit in Court. 
20. So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioner, the first respondent was the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-AH-5721 and he is her husband, the second respondent is the owner of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18-EE-9178 and the third respondent is the insurer of the said motorcycle. The respondents No.1 and 2 have remained exparte. The third respondent has admitted that it has issued policy in favour of the second respondent with respect to the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18- EE-9178. RW.1 has produced the insurance policy at Ex.R.2.
21. RW.1 has stated that the insured motorcycle was not at all responsible for the alleged accident,
since the jurisdictional police have filed the chargesheet against the first respondent who was the rider of the motorcycle in which the petitioner was a pillion rider. RW.1 has also deposed that as the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the first respondent, the third respondent is not a necessary party to the proceedings and the second respondent has violated the terms and conditions of the policy. As discussed in Issue Nos.1 and 2, this court has come to the conclusion that both the riders of the motorcycles i.e., respondents No.1 and 2 have equally contributed negligence in causing the accident and the contributory negligence is fixed at 50:50. 
Hence, the first respondent is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioner and the respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount to the petitioner. 
Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
8 22. The learned counsel for the petitioner during his arguments, has relied upon a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2015)9 SCC 273 (Khenyel Vs New India Assurance Co., Ltd., and Others). This decision is in respect of the composite negligence. 
23. In this regard I intend to rely upon the observations made in Para No.6 of the Judgment reported in 2008(3) SCC 748 (T.O.Antony Vs. Karvarnan & Ors.), which reads as under:
" 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons. 
Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrong doers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrong doers. In such a case, each wrong doer, is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them. In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrong doer separately, nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrong doer separately. On the other hand, where a person suffers injury, partly due to the negligence on the part of another person or persons, and partly as a result of his own negligence, then the negligence of the part of the injured which contributed to the accident is referred to as his contributory negligence. Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stands reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence." 
In view of the above principles laid down by their Lordships in the above case and in view of my finding on Issue Nos.1 and 2 that there is negligence on the part of riders of both the motorcycles to an extent of 50% each in occurrence of the accident, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is required to be paid by both the respondents No.1 & 2.
24. The facts and circumstances of the decision relied upon by the petitioner's counsel differs from the facts and circumstances of the present case. Hence, this case cannot be considered as a case of composite negligence, since in this case, there is head-on-collision between both the motorcycles and both the riders have equally contributed negligence in causing the accident. Therefore, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.3,89,000/- with interest at 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of realisation. Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative. 
25. Issue No.4 : In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 to 3, awarding compensation of Rs.3,89,000/- (Rupees three lakh eighty nine thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court. 
Rathnamma P.E vs Sathishkumar K.R on 31 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69990909/
9 The respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,94,500/- (being 50% of the total compensation of Rs.3,89,000), to the petitioner with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation and he is directed to deposit the said amount within 3 months from the date of this order. 
The respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,94,500/- (being 50% of the compensation amount of Rs.3,89,000/-) to the petitioner with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
However, the respondent No.3, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order. 
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years. Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner. 
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- . Draw an Award accordingly.

1  JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as follows:
That on 22.01.2019 at about 6.45 p.m., when the petitioner was a pillion rider in motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 along with the rider i.e., her husband on Panchanahalli-Singatagere Road, from her native place and when they reached near Veterinary hospital, at that time, one motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-18-EE-9178 being driven by its rider, came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner without caring human safety and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, due to this impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

annotations.text: This decision is in respect of the composite negligence.

23. In this regard I intend to rely upon the observations made in Para No.6 of the Judgment reported in 2008(3) SCC 748 (T.O.Antony Vs. Karvarnan & Ors.), which reads as under:
" 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons.
Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrong doers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrong doers.
In such a case, each wrong doer, is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them.

In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrong doer separately, nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrong doer separately.

On the other hand, where a person suffers injury, partly due to the negligence on the part of another person or persons, and partly as a result of his own negligence, then the negligence of the part of the injured which contributed to the accident is referred to as his contributory negligence.

Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stands reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence."

In view of the above principles laid down by their Lordships in the above case and in view of my finding on Issue Nos.1 and 2 that there is negligence on the part of riders of both the motorcycles to an extent of 50% each in occurrence of the accident, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is required to be paid by both the respondents No.1 & 2.

summary.ANALYSIS:
The first respondent being the owner of the motorcycle in which the petitioner was a pillion rider has remained exparte.
RW.1 in his cross- examination has admitted that accident took place due to head-on-collision between both the motorcycles and as per IMV report, both the motorcycles are damaged.
Hence, it can be said that there was head-on-collision between both the vehicles.

If really the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the complainant i.e., the second respondent, then, the first respondent being the husband of the petitioner, would have challenged the charge sheet filed against him.
But the first respondent has not challenged the chargesheet.
This conduct of the first respondent enables the court to hold that as the accident took place due to his negligence also, he has remained silent.
Even this fact creates doubt about the case put forth by the petitioner regarding occurring of the accident solely due to the negligence of the second respondent.
It is the bounden duty of both the riders to ride the motorcycles by observing the vehicles moving on the road by taking care and caution.
But, in the present case, both the riders of the motorcycles have ridden their motorcycles without taking any care and caution and this has resulted in head-on-collision between both the motorcycles.
The documents placed before the court clearly establish that there was head-on-collision between both the motorcycles and as such, both the riders of the motorcycles are negligent in causing the accident.
16.
Hence, it can be said that both the riders of the motorcycles have contributed negligence in causing of the accident.
Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of both the motorcycles i.e., both the respondents No.1 and 2 in causing the accident.

Hence, the first respondent is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioner and the respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount to the petitioner.

Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
